findings.claim: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count/last_match_at inside email validation, and users#create runs validations twice (user.valid? then user.save), so one signup attempt is counted twice and causes extra writes.

verifier.reason: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count, sets last_match_at, and saves the record (app/models/blocked_email.rb:11-19), and is called from EmailValidator#validate_each (lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13, wired on User at app/models/user.rb:47). Because UsersController#create evaluates user.valid? (app/controllers/users_controller.rb:168) and then calls user.save (app/controllers/users_controller.rb:172) while email_changed? is still true, a single signup attempt triggers email validation twice, double-counting match_count and issuing an extra write.

findings.claim: pushObject(result.values.email) adds null/undefined to rejectedEmails when the server response omits or blanks values.email.

verifier.reason: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:274-275, the guard checks result.errors && result.errors.email && result.values without verifying result.values.email, so pushObject(result.values.email) pushes undefined, null, or "" into rejectedEmails when the server omits or blanks values.email (e.g., app/controllers/users_controller.rb:199 returns nil/blank email when params[:email] is missing or empty). Impact is limited because emailValidation in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:61-74 returns early when accountEmail is blank before calling rejectedEmails.contains(email).

findings.claim: EmailValidator no longer rejects malformed addresses, so validates :email, email: true accepts values like sam@sam or sam.

verifier.reason: EmailValidator#validate_each in lib/validators/email_validator.rb:3-16 only checks SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist, SiteSetting.email_domains_blacklist, and BlockedEmail.should_block?, performing no email format validation (such as Email.is_valid? in lib/email.rb:9-16). Because app/models/user.rb:46-47 only validates :email with presence, uniqueness, and email: true, malformed addresses like sam@sam or sam are accepted under default settings.

findings.claim: The 'last_match_at is null' example tests an ActiveRecord/migration default rather than application logic.

verifier.reason: In spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:12-16, the 'last_match_at is null' example only calls BlockedEmail.create(email: email) and asserts last_match_at is nil, while app/models/blocked_email.rb:21-23 only sets action_type in set_defaults and never touches last_match_at outside should_block? (app/models/blocked_email.rb:15). Thus the example only checks the default null value of the database/ActiveRecord column rather than any application logic.
